exercises.prompt:
What does this code print?

```vb
Dim items As New List(Of Integer) From {4, 8, 15}
items.Add(16)
items.Insert(1, 23)
items.Remove(8)
Console.WriteLine(String.Join(",", items))
```

feedback.message: Not yet — `Remove(8)` removes the *value* 8, wherever it is.
Not yet — `Insert(1, ...)` inserts at index 1, after the first element.

hints: Trace the list after each call.
`Remove` removes by value; `RemoveAt` removes by position.

exercises.prompt:
What does this code print?

```vb
Dim q = From n In {5, 3, 8, 1} Where n > 2 Order By n Select n * 10
Console.WriteLine(String.Join(" ", q))
```

feedback.message: Not yet — the `Order By` clause sorts the numbers before they are selected.

hints: Keep the numbers above 2, sort them, then multiply by 10.
exercises.solution: The numbers above 2 are 5, 3 and 8; ordered, 3, 5, 8; times 10: `30 50 80`.

exercises.prompt:
What does this code print?

```vb
Dim words = {"sun", "rain", "wind", "fog", "storm"}
Dim longOnes = Aggregate w In words Where w.Length > 3 Into Count()
Console.WriteLine(longOnes)
```
hints: Which words have more than three letters?
exercises.solution: `rain`, `wind` and `storm` have more than three letters, so the aggregate count is **3**.

exercises.prompt:
What does this program print?

```vb
Option Strict On

Module Program
    Sub Main()
        Dim numbers As New List(Of Integer) From {1, 2, 3}
        Dim bigOnes = From n In numbers Where n > 1 Select n
        numbers.Add(10)
        Console.WriteLine(bigOnes.Count())
    End Sub
End Module
```

feedback.message: Not yet — the query does not run when it is written. When does it run, and what does the list contain then?

hints: A query runs when it is enumerated, here by `Count()`.
By then, the list holds 1, 2, 3 and 10.
exercises.solution: The query is evaluated when `Count()` runs, after 10 has been added. The numbers above 1 are then 2, 3 and 10, so it prints **3**.

exercises.prompt:
What does this program print?

```vb
Option Strict On

Module Program
    Sub Main()
        Dim order = <order id="A17"><line qty="2">tea</line><line qty="5">sugar</line></order>
        Dim total = Aggregate l In order.<line> Into Sum(CInt(l.@qty))
        Console.WriteLine($"{order.@id} {total}")
    End Sub
End Module
```
hints: `order.<line>` is the sequence of `line` child elements.
`l.@qty` is the text of the `qty` attribute.
exercises.solution: `order.@id` is `A17`. The query sums the `qty` attributes of the two `line` elements, 2 + 5 = 7. Output: `A17 7`.

exercises.prompt: An old import routine checks, for each of 200,000 incoming customer codes, whether the code is already in a `List(Of String)` of known codes, using `knownCodes.Contains(code)`. It has become very slow. What is the best fix?

options.label: Store the known codes in a `HashSet(Of String)` and keep calling `Contains`
options.feedback: Yes. A hash set answers membership in about constant time, so the routine becomes linear instead of quadratic.

options.label: Sort the list before each call to `Contains`
options.feedback: Not yet — `Contains` on a list still scans it, and sorting it each time adds even more work.

options.label: Use `ReDim Preserve` on an array instead of a list
options.feedback: Not yet — an array has the same linear search problem, and resizing it is slower still.

options.label: Rewrite the loop as a LINQ query with `Where`
options.feedback: Not yet — a query over a list still performs a linear search for each code.

hints: How long does `Contains` take on a list of n items?
Which collection answers "is this present?" in about constant time?
exercises.solution: `List.Contains` scans the list, so 200,000 checks against a growing list is quadratic work. A `HashSet(Of String)` makes each check take about constant time, often turning minutes into fractions of a second. This is one of the most valuable small changes in old code.
